recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — audit entity query (findByEntity / getByEntity)
recommended_phases.rationale: Innermost dependency; nothing else can be built or tested until the audit module can read by entity. Four files, all in src/modules/audit/: add findByEntity(entityType, entityId, client?) to IAuditRepository and PgAuditLogRepository (SELECT the existing COLUMNS WHERE entity_type = $1 AND entity_id = $2 ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, reusing mapRow/parseState and the optional trailing PoolClient convention), and getByEntity(entityType, entityId) to IAuditService and AuditService (validate non-empty entityType/entityId with ValidationError, delegate to the repository, return [] rather than throwing when there are no rows). No route, no leave change, no new module, no shared-types change. Unit-testable in isolation with an in-memory fake repository.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.getHistory (visibility via existing getById)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on Phase 1 only. Add getHistory(actor, requestId) to ILeaveService and LeaveService in src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts. It MUST call the existing this.getById(actor, requestId) first and let it throw — that is the single place the visibility rule (ADMIN all; MANAGER own + direct reports; anyone else own) is expressed, and it already produces the byte-identical NotFoundError for invisible and nonexistent ids. Do NOT re-derive visibility here and do NOT branch on EmployeeRole. Then delegate to this.auditService.getByEntity('leave_request', requestId) and return the entries oldest-first. Read-only: no uow.withTransaction, no client forwarding, no writes. The 'leave_request' entityType literal is the leave module's own value, matching what create/submit/approve/reject/cancel already write.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — GET /leaves/:id/history route
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on Phase 2. Add GET /leaves/:id/history (200) to leaveRoutes in src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts, mirroring the existing GET /leaves/:id handler exactly: resolveActor(request) at the API boundary, request.params.id, leaveService.getHistory(actor, id), reply.status(200).send(entries), try/catch -> request.log.error -> sendError. Reuse the existing resolveActor and sendError helpers — do not add a second copy and do not add a controller file. No role guard is added: the service's getById call is the authorization, and a caller who may not see the request receives the SAME 404 NotFoundError (never 403), so the endpoint does not leak existence. An existing-but-invisible request and a nonexistent id must produce byte-identical responses.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — tests: entity-query ordering, endpoint visibility, empty history
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on Phases 1–3. (a) tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.service.test.ts — extend the existing suite with getByEntity: ordering is the repository's contract, so assert the service delegates entityType/entityId verbatim, returns [] for no rows, and throws ValidationError on empty entityType/entityId; add a repository-level ordering test (in-memory fake or a query-shape assertion) pinning occurredAt ASCENDING. (b) tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts — extend the existing route suite (the leaveService decoration seam) with GET /leaves/:id/history: the request's own employee gets 200 with the entries; a MANAGER reading a direct report's history gets 200; a requester who may not see the request gets 404 with code NOT_FOUND, byte-identical to the nonexistent-id response; and an existing visible request with no audit rows gets 200 with []. The fake ILeaveService must implement getHistory alongside the existing methods.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries (extend, do not contradict, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

- **Presentation** — `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts`. `GET /leaves/:id/history` handler only: `resolveActor`, `request.params.id`, call the service, `reply.status(200).send(entries)`, `try/catch -> request.log.error -> sendError`. No controller file (binding rule 5, unchanged). No SQL, no business logic, no role branch.
- **Application** — `LeaveService.getHistory(actor, requestId)` (orchestration + visibility) and `AuditService.getByEntity(entityType, entityId)` (entity-scoped read). Both declared on their interfaces before implementation.
- **Domain** — `AuditLog` (audit, lifecycle RECORDED) and `LeaveRequest` (leave). No new domain type is introduced by this feature.
- **Infrastructure** — `PgAuditLogRepository.findByEntity` (the only place the entity query is written), `PgLeaveRequestRepository` (unchanged), `src/shared/db` pool.

Dependencies flow inward: routes -> service interfaces -> repository interfaces -> shared-db. No new edge is added by this feature; every edge in the dependency map already exists.

## Ownership (the load-bearing constraint)

The visibility rule (ADMIN all; MANAGER own + direct reports; anyone else own) is owned by `leave` and is expressed in exactly one place: the existing `LeaveService.getById`. `getHistory` calls it first and lets it throw. The audit module gains a purely mechanical `entityType + entityId` query and **never** branches on `EmployeeRole` — HARNESS.json declares `EmployeeRole` an owned decision whose owners are `leave` and `web-leave`, and the constraint check flags comparisons on lines the phase writes. The route adds no role guard either: authorization is the service's `getById` call, and the 404 it already produces is the response for both invisible and nonexistent ids (no 403, no existence leak).

## Concerns to surface (not resolved by ignoring the existing document)

1. **The discovery pass for this feature was terminated early with no findings transmitted.** Everything above is derived from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md`, `HARNESS.json` and the current source, not from a completed investigation. Treat any claim about files not read here as unverified.
2. **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` records the audit module's repository/service interfaces as `create`/`findById` and `record`/`getById` only.** This feature extends both interfaces, so the audit module's documented surface is now stale and must be updated in the same change — the doc is the contract the dependency check and later features read.
3. **`AuditLog` is the required response shape but is an audit-owned entity with lifecycle state.** It must not be promoted to `src/shared/types/` (it is not a methodless cross-module DTO) and must not be re-declared in `leave`. Recorded as an open question for the design agent rather than resolved here.
4. **Ordering ties are unspecified.** `occurredAt ASCENDING` alone is not a total order; recorded as an open question because the rule must hold for every consumer of `findByEntity`, not just this endpoint (the BR-001 anti-pattern).
5. **GP-002 is not engaged.** This feature is read-only: it writes no audit record, opens no transaction, and forwards no `PoolClient`. The existing `IUnitOfWork` contract is untouched.
6. **No new module, no new shared type, no schema change.** `audit_logs` already carries the `(entity_type, entity_id)` index the query needs (recorded in the GP-008 feature's table spec), so no migration is required.

## Phases

1. audit entity query (4 files) — innermost, unit-testable alone.
2. `LeaveService.getHistory` (1 file) — depends on 1.
3. `GET /leaves/:id/history` route (1 file) — depends on 2.
4. Tests: ordering, own-employee, MANAGER-on-direct-report, invisible -> 404, empty history (2 files) — depends on 1–3.

Each phase is 1–4 files, well inside `planner.maxFilesPerPhase` (5) and Aider's effective context window.

open_questions.question: Tie-break when two audit rows for the same entity share an identical occurredAt (same-millisecond writes, e.g. a create and a follow-up update in the same millisecond, or a future multi-entry transaction).
open_questions.impact: The requirement fixes only 'ordered by occurredAt ASCENDING'. If the tie-break is left unspecified, the same request's history can come back in a different order on two reads (PostgreSQL gives no stable order for equal sort keys), so the endpoint is non-deterministic and the ordering test is flaky. This is a foundational ordering rule that must hold for every consumer of findByEntity, not just one call site.
candidate_options: ORDER BY occurred_at ASC only (accept non-determinism for ties)
ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, id ASC (deterministic, but id is a random UUID so the tie order is arbitrary yet stable)
ORDER BY occurred_at ASC, then a monotonic insertion sequence column (requires a schema change)

open_questions.question: What is the declared return type of ILeaveService.getHistory — the audit module's AuditLog entity, or a leave-owned projection?
open_questions.impact: The required response shape { id, actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState, occurredAt } is exactly the existing AuditLog entity, which has lifecycle state (RECORDED) and is owned by the audit module. Per the placement rule it must NOT be promoted to src/shared/types/ and must NOT be re-declared in leave. The design agent must therefore decide whether getHistory returns AuditLog[] directly or maps to a leave-owned projection; a second declaration of the same shape would create two sources of truth for the wire contract.
candidate_options: Return the audit module's AuditLog entity as-is (no new type; the route serializes it)
Declare a LeaveHistoryEntry DTO in src/shared/types/ (cross-module shape, but only leave consumes it today)
Declare a module-local LeaveHistoryEntry in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts

open_questions.question: Should the history response be bounded when a leave request accumulates a large number of audit entries?
open_questions.impact: Pagination and filtering are explicitly out of scope, so the endpoint returns the full trail. A long-lived request (create, submit, approve, cancel, plus any future reversal entries) is bounded in practice, but the endpoint has no cap. If a request's audit trail can grow without bound, the response size is unbounded and the endpoint becomes a memory/latency risk. Recording it keeps the decision explicit rather than accidental.
candidate_options: No limit — return every entry (matches the stated out-of-scope for pagination)
A fixed server-side cap with no client control
Defer entirely; revisit if a request's history grows unbounded

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role come from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role; only /auth/login is in PUBLIC_PATHS, so GET /leaves/:id/history requires a valid token. The route-level resolveActor helper (reused unchanged from leave.routes.ts) extracts request.user and enforces id presence plus EmployeeRole membership at the API boundary, throwing UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor. RBAC is NOT enforced inline in the route and no role guard is added: the endpoint's authorization is the service's existing LeaveService.getById(actor, requestId) call, which owns the visibility rule (ADMIN sees all; MANAGER sees own plus direct reports, one level only; anyone else only own) and throws NotFoundError for a request the caller may not see. No new role, no new claim, no change to the identity shape.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string } via the existing sendError helper (AppError -> its statusCode + code; any other throw -> 500 { error: 'Internal Server Error' }). GET /leaves/:id/history: validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION) for a malformed entityType/entityId reaching the audit service; authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED) for a missing or invalid actor; authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN) is NOT produced by this endpoint — a caller who may not see the request receives the SAME 404 as a nonexistent id, so existence is never leaked; not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND) for both an invisible and a nonexistent request, byte-identical. Success: 200 with an array of { id, actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState, occurredAt } ordered oldest first; an existing, visible request with no audit rows returns 200 with [] (never 404). No 409 is produced (read-only).
